outcome: No source I found, dated after 26 January 2024 or before, gives a logic with all four properties; the nearest results each miss one condition, so as far as the sources show the bullet remains open, with the closest candidates being a 1985 compact logic with the Beth property that fails Souslin-Kleene (Δ-)interpolation and the Δ-closure of a compact logic, which has Δ-interpolation but is reported to lack the Beth property.
problem_asks: Asks for a logic L (an abstract logic; the statement does not say whether it must extend first-order logic or be regular) that together satisfies: (1) the Beth property, i.e. implicit definability implies explicit definability; (2) Δ-interpolation, which the sources call Suslin-Kleene interpolation; (3) compactness, which the statement leaves unspecified (I read it as full compactness, (κ,λ)-compactness for all κ≥λ, following the sources; an ℵ0-compactness reading is a live alternative); and (4) failure of the interpolation property (Craig). The four conditions must hold of one and the same L. A yes answer needs one such L; a no answer needs an impossibility argument.

events.what_happened: Makowsky, Shelah and Stavi, 'Δ-logics and generalized quantifiers', Annals of Mathematical Logic 10 (1976) 155-192. Introduces the Δ-closure Δ(L), the least extension of L with Δ-interpolation, and shows that it preserves compactness. The 2025 paper by Väänänen and Ur Ya'ar cites this as the source of the fact that Δ(L) is (κ,λ)-compact when L is. I did not open the 1976 paper; its content comes from search summaries and from that citing paper.
events.delivers: For any logic L, Δ(L) is the minimal extension of L with Δ-interpolation, and if L is compact then Δ(L) is compact (cited as “Δ(ℒ) is (κ,λ)-compact … if ℒ is”, §1.1 Fact 3 of arXiv:2508.07892). Gives the compact-plus-Δ-interpolation half of the bullet for a candidate logic. Restrictions: says nothing about the Beth property of Δ(L) or about Craig interpolation of Δ(L).
events.remains: Condition (1), the Beth property of Δ(L), is not addressed. Condition (4), failure of interpolation for Δ(L), is not addressed. The event does not supply a logic that satisfies all four conditions.

checked_by.qualification: Logicians working on the Δ-operation; authors of the 2025 paper that uses the fact
checked_by.what_they_did: Cite the 1976 compactness fact as Fact 3 and use it in §4; no re-derivation is given in the part of the paper I read

events.direction: Positive for the compactness and Δ-interpolation conditions of the bullet, for the Δ-closure of a compact logic. Silent on the Beth property and on interpolation.

events.what_happened: Makowsky and Shelah, 'The theorems of Beth and Craig in abstract model theory II. Compact logics', Archiv für Mathematische Logik und Grundlagenforschung 21 (1981) 13-35, published December 1981. The HUJI record abstract says it treats compact logics (stationary logic, positive logic, cardinality-quantifier and cofinality-quantifier logics), states that 'Counterexamples to the theorems of Beth and Craig are given', applies back-and-forth to the first two logics, and gives a new compactness proof for the cofinality quantifiers. The abstract does not say which logic gets which counterexample. I could not open the full text (the Springer link redirected to a login page).
events.delivers: Per the abstract, the Beth and Craig theorems fail for some of the compact logics it treats (stationary, positive, cardinality and cofinality quantifier logics). It does not produce a compact logic with the Beth property. Restriction: which logics carry the counterexamples is not stated in the abstract.
events.remains: All four conditions of the bullet remain open after this event. It bears on the bullet only as negative evidence about the Beth property in compact logics.

events.what_happened: Shelah, 'Remarks in abstract model theory', Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 29 (1985) 255-288. Cited as [Sh:199] in Shelah's Publication 750 (arXiv:0902.0439), where §0 reads: 'By [Sh:199], e.g. for λ=2^ℵ0, its Beth closure is compact, giving the first compact logic with the Beth property', the logic being the cofinality-quantifier logic L(Q^cf_{≤λ}). I could not open Sh:199 itself. The Souslin-Kleene failure reported below comes from the 2025 survey, which cites a reference it labels [50] for the Beth-closure claim; I did not confirm that [50] is this paper.
events.delivers: The Beth closure of the cofinality-quantifier logic L(Q^cf_{≤2^ℵ0}) is compact and has the Beth property, so it is a compact logic with the Beth property that is strictly stronger than first-order logic (as Sh:750 reads Sh:199). Per the 2025 survey's discussion of Proposition 14, that same Beth closure 'does not satisfy interpolation, not even Souslin-Kleene interpolation'. Restriction: the result concerns only the Beth closure of L(Q^cf_{≤2^ℵ0}), at λ = 2^ℵ0.
events.remains: Condition (2) of the bullet, Δ-interpolation (Souslin-Kleene), fails for this logic according to the survey. So this event does not supply a logic meeting the bullet. Whether another compact logic with the Beth property has Δ-interpolation and fails interpolation is not addressed.

checked_by.qualification: Logician, author of the 2025 survey that restates this result
checked_by.what_they_did: Restated the Beth-closure claim with a citation and used it to show that the converse of Craig-implies-Beth fails even with compactness; no re-derivation described

events.doubts: No independent verification found. Shelah's own restatement in Publication 750 and Väänänen's 2025 restatement both rest on the citation, not on a re-derivation I could read. The compactness half depends on compactness of L(Q^cf), and an anonymous referee of a preliminary version of Publication 750 reportedly disputed the ZFC validity of a compactness proof for L(Q^cf) (see disputes). I could not verify that dispute from the page text.
events.direction: Positive for the Beth and compactness conditions for this particular logic. Against condition (2) of the bullet for that logic, according to the survey. Does not settle the bullet.
events.object: The Beth closure of L(Q^cf_{≤2^ℵ0}), an abstract extension of the cofinality-quantifier logic. The sources I read do not describe its construction or give sentence-level content, so I cannot say whether it is explicit. Not a counterexample to any statement of the bullet.

events.what_happened: Shelah, 'On λ strongly homogeneity existence for cofinality logics' (Publication 750), arXiv:0902.0439, v1 posted February 2009; published as 'On λ strong homogeneity existence for cofinality logic', CUBO 13(2) (2011) 59-72 (publication details from search summaries, not verified on the journal page). Main result: for a nonempty class C of regular cardinals, L(Q^cf_C) has the homogeneous model existence property. §0 restates the Beth-closure fact from Sh:199 for λ=2^ℵ0. §0 says 'the situation concerning the weak Beth property is not clear' and poses a question whether L(QC^cf(1)) has the weak Beth property. It also cites Mekler-Shelah's consistency result for L(Q^card_{≥ℵ1}). The paper states that the first version of §1 was done in 1996.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 February 2009 (from search summary); CUBO 2011 published version (not verified on the journal page).
events.delivers: Establishes homogeneous model existence for L(Q^cf_C) for classes C of regular cardinals. Restates the Sh:199 Beth-closure compactness claim. Adds no new Beth or Δ-interpolation result. Restriction: concerns the cofinality-quantifier logics only.
events.remains: Condition (1), the weak Beth property for L(Q^cf_C), is left open by the paper's own question. Conditions (2) and (4) for any logic are not addressed.
events.doubts: The paper reports that an anonymous referee of a preliminary version did not accept the ZFC validity of a compactness proof for L(Q^cf) presented in a cited reference [8], apparently because of an assumed weakly compact cardinal at the start of that article. I saw this sentence only in a search summary; the ar5iv page I opened did not contain it. The paper does not say how the referee's objection was resolved. A 2019 exposition by Casanovas and Ziegler (arXiv:1903.00579) presents compactness for any set C of regular cardinals; I opened only its abstract.
events.direction: Neutral for the bullet. Restates the positive Beth-and-compact fact for one logic and records the weak Beth question for the cofinality logics as open.

events.what_happened: Väänänen, 'Interpolation in model theory', arXiv:2507.19097, submitted 25 July 2025 (v1 only). An expository survey. In §2, after Proposition 14, it restates that the Beth closure of L(Q^cof_{≤2^ω}) is compact with the Beth property but 'does not satisfy interpolation, not even Souslin-Kleene interpolation' (citing [50]), and that the Δ-closure of the same logic 'does not have the Beth property' (citing [38] and [48]). §3 lists open problems, including whether there is a countably compact proper extension of first-order logic with interpolation, and whether weak Beth holds for L(Q1) provably in ZFC. §5 asks whether some logic between L(Q^cof_ω) and L(aa) has Craig interpolation. The survey does not state a logic with all four properties of the bullet.
events.revisions: v1 only, per the arXiv abstract page
events.delivers: Reports, with citations, that the best-known compact logic with the Beth property fails Souslin-Kleene (Δ-)interpolation, and that the Δ-closure of that logic lacks the Beth property. It introduces no new result on the bullet. Restriction: it reports results from older papers whose references I could not map to titles.
events.remains: The bullet's conjunction (Beth, Δ-interpolation, compactness, no interpolation) is not claimed in the survey for any logic.
events.doubts: The survey relies on references [38], [48] and [50], whose entries I could not read, so I cannot confirm which papers they are. I found no public engagement with the survey's Proposition 14 claims.
events.direction: Reports, with citations, that the compact Beth-closure example fails Δ-interpolation, which cuts against the bullet for that example. It does not supply a counterexample to the bullet.

events.what_happened: Väänänen and Ur Ya'ar, 'Inner models from extended logics and the Delta-operation', arXiv:2508.07892. The paper I opened is v3, dated 3 March 2026, and the page lists no earlier versions. A search summary gives the first posting as 11 August 2025, which I did not verify on the arXiv page. The main topic is the inner models C(L) and C(Δ(L)). It uses the facts that Δ(L) is the minimal extension with Suslin-Kleene interpolation (Fact 3), that Δ(L) is (κ,λ)-compact when L is (Fact 3), and that Δ(L(Q1)) is ℵ0-compact (§4, Proposition 21). It never states whether Δ(L) has the Beth property.
events.revisions: v3 3 March 2026 (opened); v1 August 2025 from a search summary, not verified on the page.
events.delivers: For a compact logic L, Δ(L) is a compact logic with Δ-interpolation, by the cited Fact 3. This gives candidate compact Δ-interpolating logics. Restriction: the paper's own results are about inner models, not about the Beth property or Craig interpolation.
events.remains: Whether Δ(L) has the Beth property, and whether Δ(L) fails interpolation, for any compact L, including the Beth closure of L(Q^cf_{≤2^ℵ0}). Not addressed.
events.direction: Supports the compact-plus-Δ-interpolation half of the bullet via a cited fact. Silent on the Beth half and on interpolation.

disputes.summary: An anonymous referee of a preliminary version of Publication 750 reportedly did not accept the ZFC validity of a compactness proof for L(Q^cf) presented in a cited reference [8], apparently confused by a weakly compact cardinal assumed at the start of that article. The sentence came from a search summary; the page I opened did not contain it, and I did not find how the objection was resolved. The dispute bears on the compactness half of the Sh:199 Beth-closure claim.

summary: I ran 42 web searches and opened the Wikipedia list (current raw wikitext and rendered page), Väänänen's 2025 survey, Väänänen and Ur Ya'ar's 2025 paper, Shelah's Publication 750 (via ar5iv), Shelah's 1999 note (via ar5iv), the Makowsky-Shelah 1981 HUJI record, the Casanovas-Ziegler 2019 abstract and the Freitag-Mutchnik 2026 abstract. The bullet is in the Model theory and formal languages section, citing Makowsky, 'Compactness, embeddings and definability', in Barwise and Feferman (eds.), Model-Theoretic Logics (Springer, 1985), pp. 645-715 per the wikitext; I could not open that chapter, and other sources give pp. 645-716. The question is therefore a 1985 question. Nothing I found settles or moves the conjunction. The closest results each miss one condition. First, Shelah's [Sh:199] (APAL 1985, per Publication 750's reference list) gives the Beth closure of L(Q^cf_{≤2^ℵ0}) as compact with the Beth property; the 2025 survey reports that this same logic 'does not satisfy interpolation, not even Souslin-Kleene interpolation', so it fails condition (2). Second, the Δ-closure of a compact logic is compact and has Δ-interpolation (Makowsky-Shelah-Stavi 1976; Fact 3 of Väänänen and Ur Ya'ar 2025), but the survey reports that the Δ-closure of L(Q^cf_{≤2^ℵ0}) lacks the Beth property, so it fails condition (1). The two constructions are not combined anywhere I could find, for example by taking the Beth closure of a compact Δ-closed logic, and whether compactness and Δ-interpolation survive that combination is not stated in any source. Makowsky-Shelah 1981 gives counterexamples to Beth and Craig in several compact logics without naming them in the abstract. Shelah's 1999 note (math/9910158) asks, in its §3, whether there is a reasonably defined Q with L(Q) compact and interpolation or at least Beth (its Question 3.14 in the extraction I read); this question is open in the sources, and the survey asks neighbouring questions. No event after January 2024 addresses the bullet's conjunction. The 2025 survey and the 2025/26 Δ paper restate or extend older facts without the conjunction. The only AI-involved model-theory item in the window that I found is Freitag and Mutchnik (August 2026), on the stable forking conjecture, which is a different problem and is recorded as a discounted neighbour; its abstract says 'Using ChatGPT 5.6'. No source I read names an AI system for this bullet, and I found no machine-checked result on it: a single Lean and Beth search found only older formalisation attempts. Background I did not open: Jensen (1974) shows Craig implies Beth and Souslin-Kleene implies weak Beth, and gives a logic where Beth does not imply Souslin-Kleene; this is from search summaries and is not recorded as an event. Makowsky-Shelah 1979 (Part I) treats the interrelations of definability properties and compactness; its record is from search results only. Close calls: (a) the Souslin-Kleene failure for the Beth closure is taken from the 2025 survey, which cites a reference I could not map to Sh:199; if the survey is wrong, the Beth closure would satisfy conditions (1) to (4) with (2) holding, which would settle the bullet positively, so this is the most important claim to check. (b) Compactness: I read it as full compactness, which the Beth-closure example meets; under an ℵ0-compactness reading, Δ(L(Q1)) (ℵ0-compact by Väänänen and Ur Ya'ar's Proposition 21) becomes a candidate that needs only the Beth property and failure of Craig, and the survey lists related questions about L(Q1) as open. (c) The Freitag-Mutchnik event is recorded as a neighbour, not as evidence about this bullet.
competing_reading: The bullet might be read as already answered by the Beth closure of L(Q^cf_{≤2^ℵ0}), if the survey's 'not even Souslin-Kleene interpolation' is a mis-citation or refers to a different logic, since Shelah's Sh:199 claim as reported in Publication 750 gives Beth plus compactness, and the bullet's remaining condition (failure of full interpolation) is what the survey asserts. Read this way, the bullet would be settled yes, but only if the Δ-interpolation failure claim is wrong. A second reading: under ℵ0-compactness, Δ(L(Q1)) might satisfy the bullet if it has the Beth property and fails Craig, which nothing I read shows.
what_would_settle_it: (1) Shelah's Sh:199 ('Remarks in abstract model theory', APAL 29, 1985), to check whether the Beth closure of L(Q^cf_{≤2^ℵ0}) fails Souslin-Kleene interpolation; this is the single most important check. (2) The 1985 Makowsky chapter (pp. 645-715) that Wikipedia cites, to see the exact problem and the examples it discusses. (3) References [38], [48] and [50] in Väänänen's 2025 survey, to confirm which papers carry the Beth-closure and Δ-closure claims. (4) A proof or refutation that the Beth closure of a compact Δ-closed logic, or the Δ-closure of a compact Beth logic, keeps compactness, Beth and Δ-interpolation while failing Craig interpolation. (5) If the bullet is read with ℵ0-compactness, whether Δ(L(Q1)) has the Beth property and fails Craig interpolation.

events.ai_basis: Using ChatGPT 5.6, we find a counterexample to the stable forking conjecture.

judgement.why: The statement asks for one logic having all four properties together (Beth, Δ-interpolation, compactness, failure of Craig interpolation). No event exhibits such a logic or proves one cannot exist. Each event supplies some of the properties for some logic, gives counterexamples to Beth, or restates older facts. None of them settles a restriction of the question, so all are scope none. That includes the Sh:199 Beth closure, which by the survey's account fails Δ-interpolation. The Freitag–Mutchnik paper is about a different conjecture. I mark it variant, so it cannot count for this problem. Its AI role is recorded only for that paper's own result.
judgement.doubts: The survey's claim that the Beth closure of L(Q^cf_{≤2^ℵ0}) fails Souslin-Kleene interpolation rests on a citation the researcher could not map. If that claim were wrong, the 1985 logic might answer the question, but it would still be a pre-snapshot event. The record also leaves open whether 'compact' means full compactness or ℵ0-compactness.
judgement.by: judging pass (JUDGE.md), claude-opus-5-5; not the researching agent and not a human reviewer
